 Police investigate after Javits Frimpong (inset) was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News; Courtesy of Thomas Frimprong) 
 By Kerry Burke | kburke@nydailynews.com | New York Daily News, Julian Roberts-Grmela and Rocco Parascandola | rparascandola@nydailynews.com | New York Daily News PUBLISHED: October 29, 2026 at 11:29 AM EDT | UPDATED: October 29, 2026 at 8:58 PM EDT A 15-year-old boy, a quiet immigrant from Ghana in the U.S. just one year, was fatally shot in the Bronx Thursday morning just steps from his home, police said.
 The teen, Javits Frimpong, was struck in the abdomen around 9:24 a.m. on Crotona Place near E. 171st St., just one block south of where he lived, in Mott Haven. 
 Police investigate after a 15-year-old boy was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News) 
 He was on his way to school at Dream Yard Preparatory School, just an 18-minute walk away on the other side of Claremont Park, when he was ambushed by three masked attackers who shot him once and fled, according to witnesses.
 Frimpong was rushed to St. Barnabas Hospital, where he underwent surgery and was initially believed to be in stable condition. But he died a short time later, police said.
 Police investigate after a 15-year-old boy was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News) 
 The victim was the intended target of the suspects — three males, each wearing a surgical mask, according to cops.
 They ran off, possibly into nearby Crotona Park , police said, and are being sought.
 Video footage obtained by the Daily News appears to show Javits Frimpong (center, brown hoodie) running from three people, one of whom is pictured at right (in black), after he was shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Obtained by Daily News) 
 Witnesses from a homeless shelter across from where Frimpong was struck said that after hearing the gunshot they rushed out along with the place’s manager to find the youth sprawled on his side, bleeding out on the street.
 A 59-year-old resident of the shelter, whose windows overlook the scene, who didn’t give his name said he saw the whole incident unfold.
 “They were waiting for him in the park,” he said. “They wore hoodies and masks. I saw him running, I heard the shot and went down.
 “The manager of the shelter asked if he was shot. He said, ‘I don’t know. I don’t know.’ There was blood all over his white T-shirt. She was applying pressure and he was going in and out of consciousness.
 Video footage obtained by the Daily News appears to show Javits Frimpong (right, brown hoodie) running from three people, one of whom is pictured at left (in black), after he was shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Obtained by Daily News) 
 “It was a pack of kids. It was one shot,” said Frederick Wiedman, 62, another shelter resident.
 “He fell on the sidewalk by the Nissan, over there. A car alarm went off and people started screaming.”
 Wiedman said police were calling for a “wagon,” but the ambulance didn’t come fast enough, so they put Frimpong in a police van and rushed him to the hospital.
 “The kid wasn’t moving,” he said. “The cops got him up and into a police van. At least they got him out of here — and quick.
 “It’s sad. These kids with guns are out of control.”
 Police investigate after a 15-year-old boy was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News) 
 The victim’s father, Thomas Frimpong, 60, said he received a call in the morning from the school’s principal breaking the news his son had been shot. He rushed to the hospital to be by his son’s side, only for the boy to die after emergency surgery could not save him.
 The father, a yellow cab driver, said teens at the school had been fighting his son and bullying him, though he stopped short of accusing them in the killing.
 He last saw his son Thursday morning as he was leaving for work, since he would always wake the boy to lock the door behind him since they share one key.
 “I don’t know anything,” he said about why his son was killed. “Only I got a call that the principal told me that my son had been shot.”
 Thomas Frimpong, father of Javits Frimpong, speaks to the media after his son was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Kerry Burke / New York Daily News) 
 He described the victim as quiet and shy, saying, “My son is very quiet. My son didn’t talk. He don’t talk. The school can testify. My son is always quiet, always, always.”
 “He scared talking to me,” he said. “Always on his phone. Every time he comes from school, he just go to my bedroom, sitting there looking at his phone, playing games, and I say at times, I ask him, ‘Javits, go out, go to the park.’ He never step outside. Even, even the hall. Even, even the living room. He will never go and sit at the living room.”
 Police investigate after a 15-year-old boy was fatally shot near E. 171st St. and Crotona Place in the Bronx on Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026. (Theodore Parisienne / New York Daily News) 
 Thomas Frimpong, who moved to New York City around 2000, has several other children living in other states, but Javits was his only child that lived here. He said Javits moved to New York only about one year ago.
 He called Javits’s mother in Ghana to inform her of the sad news.
 “I just called the mother,” he said. “I can hear her voice crying, crying, crying. All the family members are crying.”
